title: One client floods the API
question: Eight well-behaved clients share the API with one that suddenly sends 4,000 req/s. Who pays?
explain: Without per-client limits, capacity goes to whoever sends the most, so the flood pushes the origin past capacity and every client's requests time out together. A token bucket per client (400 req/s, burst 200) stops the flood at the edge, before it costs the origin anything.
traffic: 8 clients x 150 req/s of API calls; client 9 sends 4,000 req/s from 8s to 22s. Origin capacity is about 2,300 req/s.
